newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CIM says losing interest in Cumnock.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CIM says losing interest in Cumnock.

text.p: CIM Resources Ltd said on Thursday it was losing interest in a potential partnership or acquisition of fellow Hunter Valley coal miner Cumnock Coal Ltd .
"Our level of interest in Cumnock has dropped away," CIM managing director Michael Palmer told Reuters.
"Nothing much is happening there and we are looking at some other possibilities now (mostly in the Hunter Valley)", he said.
CIM said in late July that it wanted a longer term relationship with Cumnock, in which it has a 5.01 percent stake, and would consider a takeover bid.

Palmer said CIM's declining interest in Cumnock, which has semi-coking and thermal coal operations, was due to the attitude taken by major shareholder and Swiss commodities group Glencore Ag in talks over the last month or so.
Glencore has a 25.14 percent stake in Cumnock and described itself as a long term investor after its takeover bid failed earlier in 1996.
"The major shareholder in Cumnock is not interested in a sensible deal," Palmer said.
He said CIM could make an announcement on its new expansion plans in the next three to six months.
Based on Tuesday's closing price of A$2.22 per share, a bid for Cumnock would cost around A$69.52 million.

CIM has said it could afford acquisitions up to a total of A$300 million, in equal portions of debt and equity, with much of the equity funding derived from an recent investment by British coal group RJB Plc.

Palmer said CIM was not interested in a takeover of Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd which is the subject of rival bids by Centennial Coal Ltd and Hong Kong's power station group Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd.
